query:
Violations of the law must be prosecuted, but there is almost no punishment for violations of morality. If this becomes a routine, the people will lose their moral constraints. The threat of moral runaway to social stability is no less than that of law. Therefore, in order to maintain social stability, any violation of morality can not go unpunished.

The most appropriate evaluation of the above argument is that it has loopholes, which exaggerates the social harm of moral violations.
